title: A localization of a regular local ring at a prime is a regular local ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme] and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ a prime ideal. Then the localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a regular local ring. Consequently every regular local ring is a regular ring in the sense of [def-weil-regular-scheme] (all its localizations at primes are regular local rings).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AFS (lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular, line 27126), second sentence, and the remark after it leading to Definition Tag 00OD (definition-regular); proof via finite global dimension (Propositions 00O7, 00OC, Lemma 00O8 localize-finite-gl-dim)

proof.text: $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a Noetherian local ring. The regular local ring $R$ is Noetherian by definition [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The map $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}R$, $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ (a multiplicative subset since $\mathfrak p$ is prime), is the localization of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], so it satisfies (a), (b), (c) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] for $S$, and $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AFS (lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular, line 27126), proof ('any localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$', a Noetherian local ring as needed to apply Proposition 00OC); Lemma Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence) for Noetherianity

proof.text: $R$ has finite global dimension: with $d=\dim R$, every $R$-module has a projective resolution of length $\le d$, by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-finite-gl-dim] applied to the regular local ring $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AFS (lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular, line 27126), proof, first sentence (direction 'regular local implies finite global dimension' via Proposition Tag 00O7)

proof.text: $R_{\mathfrak p}$ has finite global dimension. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-finite-gl-dim], part (2), with the multiplicative subset $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $n=d$: since $R$ has global dimension $\le d$ (Step 2), $S^{-1}R=R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] has global dimension $\le d$, in particular finite global dimension [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AFS (lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular, line 27126), proof, second sentence ('any localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ has finite global dimension, see Lemma 00O8')

proof.text: $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a regular local ring: it is a Noetherian local ring (Step 1) of finite global dimension (Step 3), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-gl-dim-regular-local] applies and gives that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. This is the first assertion.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AFS (lemma-localization-of-regular-local-is-regular, line 27126), proof, end ('and hence is a regular local ring', via Proposition Tag 00OC)

proof.text: Consequence. $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-regular-scheme] and, by Steps 1-4 applied to each prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $R$, every localization $R_{\mathfrak p}$ at a prime is a regular local ring; this is the definition of a regular ring in [def-weil-regular-scheme]. (For $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$ the localization $R_{\mathfrak m}$ is isomorphic to $R$, so the two notions do not conflict.)
